task: Optimize ThreeRuntime code organization into cohesive small modules
platform: Windows Chromium SwiftShader browser; not Tauri desktop or macOS acceptance

preserved: Public ThreeRuntime exports, commands, diagnostics and caller integration
EditorCore ownership of immutable formal data and revision snapshots
Preview/commit separation, one history record per completed gesture
Existing snapping, current-floor picking, ghost display and clean export
Unrelated dirty workspace changes and pinned Skills
owners: Picking, preview tokens and transient meshes
Formal building meshes, resource leases and ChangeSet sync
Selection helpers, grid, snap marker, lights and shadows
Transient door animations and snapshot sampling
Renderer switching, postprocessing, PNG and demand-driven scheduling
Environment decode/version and clean path-tracing snapshots
Path-tracing sampling sessions and pinned backend driver adapters

reviews.architecture: Narrow explicit owner interfaces; no whole-runtime mutable host, inheritance or mechanical state splitting. Public API unchanged.
fixed: Selection helpers have idempotent teardown and cannot rebuild after their owner is disposed.
Decoration owner detaches all three owned lights and disposes directional shadow targets as well as helper geometry/materials.
Awaited path sample success/failure after rendering disposal cannot publish status, count a retained frame or schedule another RAF.
reviews.testMaintenance: The theme test expected two lights; the pre-refactor source already has two DirectionalLights plus one HemisphereLight. The next run also exposed its probe overwriting the color scene record during GTAO normal prepasses (temporary clear color 7777ff). Assert all three types/identities and observe only non-override color scene passes while retaining postprocessing, exact background token, material, exposure and document equality checks.

unchangedUiFailure.test: invalid environment values and corrupt HDR show one visible error inside the settings dialog while preserving project data
unchangedUiFailure.failure: At tests/rendering-ui.browser.spec.ts:281, the page has two role=alert elements instead of one.
unchangedUiFailure.cause: App viewport notice and RenderingSettings dialog both render the same notice.error; both branches exist in HEAD and were not changed by this refactor.
unchangedUiFailure.boundary: Core rejects intensity 11 before publishing. Independent real-Core probe: environment.invalid, document identity unchanged, zero notifications/undo/redo. Runtime sync is not invoked.
unchangedUiFailure.partialCoverage: The case stops at the alert count. Its later rotation, corrupt HDR and English assertions were not executed in this run.
unchangedUiFailure.disposition: Preserve unrelated UI source and original assertion; report as verification failure, not as an environment block or passing runtime test.

commands.warning: Existing Vite chunk-size warning remains; no bundle-size or speed improvement claim.

browser.server: Owned e2e Vite servers 1421 for regressions and 1422 for resource cycles; no reuse of user dev session
browser.engine: Chromium, software SwiftShader WebGL; unsupported WebGPU fallback covered, native hardware WebGPU not covered

browser.sourceTiming: The broad run and resource cycles started before the final small teardown fixes. Production logic is stable for the final five-case rerun and final 262-unit/type/check/build verification; the theme-only rerun adds the corrected observation probe. No claim that every broad case ran against an immutable final source snapshot.
browser.console: Passing cases retain their original page/WebGL/TSL/validation error assertions. Resource-cycle console/page/report errors are empty. Pinned libraries emit deprecation warnings (Clock, maxLeafTris and WebGLPathTracer); not described as warning-free.

resourceCycles.limitation: Counters and stable UUID identities are browser resource evidence, not native VRAM byte measurements or device-loss acceptance.

finalVisualEvidence.review: Inspected both actual 900x600 wall screenshots: connected L walls, finite line/endpoint feedback, metre readout and visible snap state; no new UI source changes.

performance.statement: This task changes ownership and code organization. No new FPS, latency or performance improvement conclusion. Parallel software-GPU test duration is not a benchmark.
performance.priorSnappingEvidence: docs/snapping-validation.json remains historical evidence for the earlier completed feature.
